::: {#sol-reverse}

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
with torch.no_grad():
    x_reversed = embed(line.flip(1))
    reversed_out, _ = attend(x_reversed, x_reversed, x_reversed)
reverse_gap = (reversed_out - self_out.flip(1)).abs().max().item()
print(reverse_gap)
```

The outputs come out in reverse order and are otherwise unchanged:
the largest difference between the new outputs and the old ones reversed is `r sprintf("%.1g", py$reverse_gap)`,
a rounding error.
Each character's output is a weighted average whose weights depend on the vectors and not on where they sit,
so [self-attention](#def-self-attention) on its own cannot tell `"First Citizen"` from `"nezitiC tsriF"`.

:::
